title: When the Group Chat Burns
premise: Elodie Thornbury, a scholarship student at Ashgrove Academy, is paired with her nemesis, wealthy legacy student Cassian Voss, for a semester-long archival project. Digging through the school's records, they uncover that the academy's founding families built their fortune on erased students—names scrubbed from every ledger, including Elodie's own grandmother. As the administration closes ranks and the group chat of elite students turns into a weapon for surveillance and blackmail, Elodie and Cassian must decide whether to protect their futures or burn the archive's silence to the ground. In the end, they leak the restored names during the spring showcase, sacrificing Cassian's inheritance and Elodie's quiet exit, but winning back the memory the school tried to bury.
about_author: August Underhill is the pen name of a former boarding-school archivist who spent three years cataloguing documents no one was supposed to read. They write stories about teenagers who refuse to be footnotes.

chapters.title: Counting Days
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. She maps her remaining days at Ashgrove like a prison sentence, surviving on scholarship grit and careful invisibility. A humiliating encounter with Cassian Voss in the dining hall establishes their enmity. The chapter ends with the history teacher announcing forced pairings for the semester archival project: Thornbury and Voss. Beat: resentment sharpened into dread.

chapters.title: The Ledger Room
chapters.summary: Alternating POV begins. Elodie and Cassian meet in the basement archives, trading barbs while cataloguing boxes from the school's first century. Elodie notices gaps—missing years, redacted registers, a photograph with faces inked out. Cassian, oddly, doesn't mock her curiosity. Beat: reluctant alliance formed over an anomaly neither can explain.

chapters.title: Names That Aren't There
chapters.summary: Cassian's POV. He pulls strings through his family's donor connections to access sealed records, expecting a favor to flaunt. Instead he finds his great-grandfather's signature on a document titled 'The Quiet Settlement'—payment for silence. Meanwhile the senior group chat buzzes with warnings about students who 'dig too deep.' Beat: privilege curdles into complicity.

chapters.title: Grandmother's Year
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. Cross-referencing a faded enrollment card, she discovers her grandmother attended Ashgrove under a different surname—and was expelled without record the same semester as 'The Quiet Settlement.' Grief and fury collide as she realizes the school erased her family twice. Beat: personal stakes ignite; the project becomes a reckoning.

chapters.title: Screenshot Season
chapters.summary: Dual POV. The elite group chat turns predatory: someone screenshots Elodie's late-night archive searches and posts them with mocking captions. Cassian quietly deletes the thread, revealing he has admin access he never wanted. Their first honest conversation happens over vending-machine coffee at midnight. Beat: enemies become co-conspirators; trust tentatively planted.

chapters.title: The Headmaster's Offer
chapters.summary: Cassian's POV. The headmaster summons him privately, offering a glowing recommendation letter—and his family's continued standing—in exchange for steering the project away from the settlement files. Cassian stalls, then lies to Elodie about the meeting. When she finds out via another screenshot, the alliance fractures. Beat: betrayal; power shows its price tag.

chapters.title: What Cassian Stands to Lose
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV, watching from outside. Cassian publicly defends the project before the board, burning bridges with his father, who threatens disinheritance. Elodie learns the full truth of his sacrifice and must choose between pride and partnership. She shows up at his door with the missing ledger page. Beat: forgiveness earned through witnessed cost.

chapters.title: The Lock Changes
chapters.summary: Dual POV. The archive room is rekeyed overnight; their research boxes are confiscated. A sympathetic janitor reveals the original ledgers were moved to the headmaster's private collection. Racing the clock before the spring showcase audition where projects are judged, they plan a retrieval that will get them expelled if caught. Beat: rising action peaks; no safe exits remain.

chapters.title: Audition
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV, climax. During the showcase, instead of presenting their sanitized project, Elodie and Cassian read aloud the restored names of the erased students—including her grandmother's—as the headmaster moves to cut the microphones. Students stand, phones recording, refusing the silence. The group chat, repurposed, floods with the scanned pages. Beat: catharsis; memory weaponized into witness.

chapters.title: After the Burn
chapters.summary: Alternating final entries. An independent inquiry opens; the headmaster resigns; Cassian's father cuts him off, and he stays on scholarship-adjacent aid, lighter than he's ever been. Elodie graduates—not counting days anymore but naming what she'll carry forward. The last scene: two names added side by side to a new ledger, written by their own hands. Beat: resolution; survival with its price paid and worth it.
